issues.where: śiro.hasta.pradīpikaṃ read as an agent noun
issues.problem: Structure suggests a manner: vā closes the list of offenders (cf. unit 19 'sandhic.chedikāṃ vā gobhiḥ pāṭayet', unit 7 'stenān vā śūlān ārohayeyuḥ'), so 'śiro-hasta-pradīpikam' is likely the neuter accusative of manner: 'should have [him] killed with head and hands set ablaze'. The agent-noun reading adds a further offender with no motive. Not certain; needs a person.
issues.fix: He should have killed, with head and hands set ablaze, one who desires ... or a provoker of fort, country and army.

patch.text: Reviewer doubt: because vā stands before śiro-hasta-pradīpikam (as before the manner words in units 7 and 19), the compound may be an adverbial accusative of manner ('with head and hands set ablaze') rather than one more offender; the translation keeps the draft's agent-noun reading unchanged; a person should decide (also unit 13).

issues.fix: A killer of mother, father, son, brother, teacher or ascetic he should have killed, with skinless head set ablaze.
